records.region: Washington: lower Nisqually River valley, Nisqually Reservation, Interstate 5 crossing and Nisqually Flats mouth setting.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity for the selected continuous lower Nisqually valley and its river-mouth receiving setting. This does not name the entire Nisqually River, establish a natural headwater, rename neighboring creeks or sloughs, or convert the terminal intertidal flats into a river feature.
records.completion_scope: All 4 original parts and 21 stored positions of the single stage 3 mainstem FID 9456, all 3 original part joins, the chosen interior opening and the separate source/render/stored endings have completed ordinary lower-river-valley, floodplain, mouth-marsh and tidal-flat correspondence. No necessary receiver link remains unobserved. Repeated direct map labels support Nisqually River as a bounded representative system identity.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the selected continuous lower Nisqually valley and its river-mouth receiving setting. This does not name the entire Nisqually River, establish a natural headwater, rename neighboring creeks or sloughs, or convert the terminal intertidal flats into a river feature.

scope_limits: The Nisqually River candidate is a bounded representative system identity only; accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null, with no product application.

The generalized stored line sometimes touches valley-edge slopes and crosses floodplain or marsh interiors. Ordinary connected corridor correspondence does not establish exact current channel alignment.
Both distinct endpoints lie in the mouth/intertidal-flat setting. Their present wetness, exact relationship to the bank and surveyed mouth status are unverified.
Individual source-map epochs, current flow/tidal conditions, legal naming extent and formal registry status remain unverified.

bounded_name_observations.name: Nisqually River
bounded_name_observations.role: Directly labeled lower river across the selected opening and receiving valley through the estuarine approach. Supported as the representative receiving-system identity for this bounded selection.

bounded_name_observations.name: Nisqually Flats
bounded_name_observations.role: Directly labeled terminal receiving flat component. Its name remains separate from the representative river name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Medicine Creek / McAllister Creek
bounded_name_observations.role: Separately mapped western drainage context; these labels are not aliases for the chosen Nisqually mainstem.

bounded_name_observations.name: Leschi Slough / Red Salmon Creek
bounded_name_observations.role: Separately mapped lower-valley and estuarine tributary settings. Their labels are not extended over the selected mainstem or tidal-flat ending.

terminal_observations.source_endpoint: Separately located slightly farther north in the mapped Nisqually mouth/intertidal-flat setting.
terminal_observations.render_endpoint: Separately located slightly south and east of the source endpoint in the same mouth/intertidal-flat setting, adjoining the terminal channel.
terminal_observations.stored_final_coordinate: Separately retained quantized final position in the render-ending setting; not substituted for the higher-precision render endpoint.
terminal_observations.geographic_interpretation: The final selected passage crosses the river-mouth marsh toward the adjacent intertidal flats. Stored sea metadata is retained but does not prove that either endpoint is continuously water-covered or marks an exact river mouth.
terminal_observations.limit: No exact distributary, modern bank, tide state or surveyed mouth vertex is inferred; the source and render endings are not conflated.

records.region: Southern Pacific Costa Rica: lower Coto Colorado floodplain and mangrove estuary by Zancudo, on the eastern Golfo Dulce shore.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity for the selected lower Coto Colorado river, floodplain and mangrove estuary. Golfo Dulce is the receiving gulf; Río Colorado and Río Conte remain distinct tributary names rather than synonyms.
records.completion_scope: All 4 original parts and 18 stored positions of single stage 3 mainstem FID 10742, every part join and the distinct source/render/stored endings were inspected. Ordinary connected river, floodplain, estuarine and shore-margin geography is complete with no unresolved necessary receiver or link. The representative identity is research-only.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the selected lower Coto Colorado river, floodplain and mangrove estuary. Golfo Dulce is the receiving gulf; Río Colorado and Río Conte remain distinct tributary names rather than synonyms.

scope_limits: No accepted, scalar or Korean product name is assigned; formal registry status remains unverified.
Generalized stored chords need not be water-covered at every position; no surveyed bank, present flow or tide claim is made.
The separately stored source endpoint and higher-precision render endpoint have different shoreline relationships, both preserved.
Exact image epochs and precise legal/name-transition boundaries remain unverified.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Coto Colorado
bounded_name_observations.role: Supported bounded representative river candidate; source nomenclature is combined with independently inspected continuous geographic corridor.

bounded_name_observations.name: Golfo Dulce
bounded_name_observations.role: Receiving feature only, kept distinct from the representative selected river.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Coto
bounded_name_observations.role: The botanical gazetteer calls its equivalence to Coto Colorado only possible. It is not adopted as a confirmed alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Colorado / Río Conte
bounded_name_observations.role: Separately named lower-basin tributaries in the gazetteer, not alternate spellings of the selected representative river.

terminal_observations.source_endpoint: Separately located in open lower-estuary water near the mangrove islands and northern bank.
terminal_observations.render_endpoint: Separately located on the wooded northern estuarine-bank fringe.
terminal_observations.stored_final_coordinate: Separately preserved quantized final position in the same shoreward setting; not substituted for the higher-precision render endpoint.
terminal_observations.geographic_interpretation: The selected Coto Colorado lower-estuary corridor ends at its northern bank fringe, before a complete open-gulf traverse.
terminal_observations.limit: Sea is retained as stored terminal metadata only. No exact present wet mouth, bank contact, tidal state or reconstructed original source line is asserted.

records.region: Amapá: southern alluvial approach to the lower Rio Amapá Grande and its estuarine bends near the mapped Ilha do Meio locality.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river-system identity, supported by a direct primary-map hydronym and ordinary connected geographic correspondence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Rio Amapá Grande identifies the receiving and lower selected trunk. The unnamed initial wetland/wooded approach remains unnamed as a component, and Rio Flechal remains a separate incoming river. No whole-feature scalar or product label is applied.
records.completion_scope: All 8 original parts and 23 positions of mainstem FID11620/stage 3 and FID11621/stage 2, every original part join, the fragment join, selected opening and separate source/render/stored endings have completed ordinary connected floodplain, river, confluence and estuarine-bank correspondence. This is not a reconstruction of an exact contemporary wet route.
records.supported_name_scope: Rio Amapá Grande identifies the receiving and lower selected trunk. The unnamed initial wetland/wooded approach remains unnamed as a component, and Rio Flechal remains a separate incoming river. No whole-feature scalar or product label is applied.

scope_limits: The opening component has no established individual hydronym; the northeast diagonal is generalized across floodplain and crosses a separate narrow lateral channel.
Map compilation dates and imagery scene dates differ and do not establish present bank positions, tide or continuous flow.
Scattered image clouds and shadows prevent claims about every surface pixel; the original municipal map supplies complementary ordinary geographic correspondence.
Ilha do Meio is read as a mapped reference locality, not assumed to be an authoritative island or river name.
The source endpoint differs from the render/stored ending; stored sea metadata is not treated as proof that the rendered path reaches the ocean shoreline.
Formal registry status and legal name extent are unverified. Accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null; application remains false.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Amapá Grande
bounded_name_observations.role: Directly mapped receiving and selected lower trunk; supported representative river-system candidate. The unnamed opening floodplain is not thereby established as a separately named Amapá Grande headwater.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Flechal
bounded_name_observations.role: Separately mapped incoming river from the south near the selected confluence. Its name is bounded to that incoming component and is not promoted as the selected trunk’s name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Ilha do Meio
bounded_name_observations.role: Map label attached to a point-of-reference symbol on the lowland enclosed by river branches. Used for orientation only; neither a river alias nor a formal island-naming determination.

terminal_observations.source_endpoint: Separately retained in the broad river water southeast of the render endpoint.
terminal_observations.render_endpoint: Separately retained at the ordinary northern river-bank and vegetated-fringe setting.
terminal_observations.stored_final_coordinate: Separately retained quantized ending in the same ordinary northern bank-fringe setting as the higher-precision render endpoint.
terminal_observations.geographic_interpretation: The selected final bend remains within the lower river and its bank margin. The mapped river continues east toward the Atlantic beyond the actual selected ending. Endpoints are not collapsed into a single river mouth or moved to the coastline.
terminal_observations.limit: No present tide, surveyed bank, salinity transition, precise river-mouth cross-section or legal hydronym boundary is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
